body.statement: For every \(p\ne q\) and every member of \(\mathcal M_s\), the counterfactual map \(C_{q\leftarrow p}\) is Euclidean monotone on \(D_p\) if and only if \(S_{pq}(u)\succeq0\) for all \(u\in\Omega\). Its sharp strong-monotonicity modulus satisfies \[\inf_{x\ne y\in D_p}\frac{\langle C_{q\leftarrow p}(x)-C_{q\leftarrow p}(y),x-y\rangle}{\lVert x-y\rVert_2^2}=\gamma_{pq}.\] In particular, \(C_{q\leftarrow p}\) is strongly Euclidean monotone if and only if \(\gamma_{pq}>0\).
body.justification: This theorem replaces mechanism-by-mechanism monotonicity with the exact cross-regime Euclidean criterion and identifies the sharp margin rather than a sufficient lower bound.
body.gap: DeLaraGanassali2025GoodMatching leaves a precise cyclic-monotonicity characterization open, while RibeiroSanthirasekaramGlocker2025DynamicOT, NeurIPS Theorem 4.12 and Appendix Theorem B.11, asserts cross-regime strict Euclidean monotonicity without the necessary cross-Hessian condition.
body.consumer: A practitioner using a Brenier counterfactual generator obtains an identified population certificate for whether its same-unit cross-regime map preserves Euclidean ranks.
